intro.title: Introduction
intro.paragraph1: In frontend development workflows, collaboration between designers and engineers is indispensable. Ideally, visual and interaction specifications delivered by designers should be implemented with pixel-perfect precision by engineers. However, several efficiency bottlenecks often exist in the design-to-development handoff:

styleRepetition.title: 1. Repetitive Style Implementation:
styleRepetition.content: Converting core design elements such as layout, typography, and colors into code consistently consumes significant engineering resources. While collaboration platforms like Figma can assist in generating partial CSS, they still struggle to automatically resolve syntax differences across Web, iOS, and Android platforms, leading to high cross-platform development and maintenance costs.

updateSync.title: 2. Synchronization Challenges:
updateSync.content: Design iterations cannot be immediately reflected in engineering code. In traditional workflows, engineers must obtain updated design files, manually compare differences through visual inspection or relying on annotations, then update code accordingly. Even more problematic, seemingly minor changes (such as adjusting a global font size) can trigger cascading effects, requiring extensive code refactoring.

whatIsDesignSystem.title: What is a Design System?
whatIsDesignSystem.paragraph1: A Design System is often referred to as the
whatIsDesignSystem.paragraph1_suffix: , consolidating all elements required for designing and developing products.
whatIsDesignSystem.quote: "A Design System is the single source of truth which groups all the elements that will allow the teams to design, realize and develop a product."
whatIsDesignSystem.paragraph2: Within this system, designers decompose interfaces into standardized components and define specifications for each component's styling, typography, color values, etc. Developers can then reference this system to obtain required components and specifications, ensuring high consistency between both parties.
whatIsDesignSystem.paragraph3: However, how does a static specification library truly solve the efficiency and synchronization problems mentioned earlier? This requires the core of design systems—

whatIsDesignToken.title: What are Design Tokens?
whatIsDesignToken.paragraph1: Design Tokens can be understood as
whatIsDesignToken.paragraph1_bold: "visual design atoms of the design system"
whatIsDesignToken.quote: "Design tokens are the visual design atoms of the design system."
whatIsDesignToken.paragraph2_bold: Abstract the most fundamental attributes in design specifications (such as colors, spacing, font sizes) and assign them platform-agnostic "names" (i.e., Tokens)
whatIsDesignToken.paragraph2_suffix: . These Tokens function like "variables" familiar to frontend developers.

platformConversion.title: This Token can then be automatically converted to formats required by different platforms:

whatIsDesignToken.paragraph3: During development, frontend engineers no longer need to manually copy color values; instead, they directly reference these semantic variables (Tokens).

repetition.content: : Developers only need to reference variables without worrying about specific values or manual platform conversions.

update.content: : When a designer decides to change the brand primary color to
update.content_suffix: Token value needs updating in the design system. All platform codebases simply import the latest Token file, and every usage of this color updates automatically, completely eliminating manual search-and-replace inefficiency.

whatIsDesignToken.summary: In summary, Design Tokens transform design systems from static documentation into dynamic, synchronizable automation bridges, truly breaking down barriers between design and development, making collaboration unprecedentedly efficient and precise.

colorNaming.title: 🎯 Color Naming Integration Guidelines for System Projects

breakdown.element: • Component (element): button, input, card, modal, table ...
breakdown.hierarchy: • Hierarchy: primary, secondary, tertiary (optional, most commonly only primary/secondary)
breakdown.state: • State: default, hover, active, disabled (omit if unused)

simplification.title: 3. Naming Simplification Guidelines
simplification.point1: If unnecessary, omit unused hierarchy levels (e.g., if most components only have primary without secondary/weak, don't add them)
simplification.point2: Common states include default, hover, active, disabled; omit if unused
simplification.point3: Global theme colors and critical colors (like system primary) can use special names like main-color or common-bg

expansion.title: 5. Continuous Expansion Recommendations
expansion.point1: The same pattern can be applied to other common components like modal, badge, etc.
expansion.point2: Only add semantic attributes (like button-bg-warning) when truly needed for warning, success states; don't force semantic abstraction unnecessarily

highlights.title: 📦 Key Points
highlights.point1: Each color variable should be immediately clear about "where it's used, what hierarchy, what state"
highlights.point2: Suitable for team collaboration, eliminating guesswork
highlights.point3: Leave room for expansion (optionally add hierarchy or state)
highlights.point4: Semantic/brand colors can be supplemented optionally, not required

implementation.title: CSS Design Tokens Implementation Architecture in Projects
implementation.intro: In our poultry farm project, we established a Design Token system highly synchronized with the design team. This system's core lies in "design collaboration" and "technical flexibility."

collaboration.title: 1. Deep Collaboration with Designers (Figma Variables):
collaboration.content: Our Token definitions aren't created arbitrarily but directly correspond to Variables maintained by designers in Figma. This ensures Design and Code use completely consistent language, significantly reducing communication costs.

business.title: 2. Business Partnership Strategy (Emotion & White-labeling):
business.content: Considering potential "white-labeling" business requirements, we chose
business.content_suffix: for style management. Through dynamic CSS Variables injection, we can quickly switch the entire site's brand theme for different business partners without modifying component code.

primitives.title: 2. Definition Layer: Figma Primitives (theme.ts)
primitives.description: This faithfully reproduces the original variable definitions from Figma, such as

semantic.title: 3. Semantic Layer: Semantic Mapping (color.ts)
semantic.description: Maps primitive colors to specific semantic purposes (like primary, surface), allowing developers to focus on "purpose" rather than "color codes" during usage.

injection.title: 4. Injection Layer: Emotion Global Styles
injection.description_suffix: component to inject computed variables into the browser. This is the key technical point for implementing "one-click theming."

integration.title: 5. Integration Layer: MUI Theme Integration
integration.description: Finally, integrate defined Tokens into MUI Theme, ensuring all ready-made components automatically inherit the latest brand design specifications.

designSync.title: Design Synchronization:
designSync.content: Variables directly correspond to Figma, eliminating design-development communication gaps.

businessFlexibility.title: Business Flexibility:
businessFlexibility.content: Emotion-based architecture enables projects to rapidly adapt to different brand identities (CI).

devConsistency.title: Development Consistency:
devConsistency.content: Through MUI Theme encapsulation, developers can directly use semantic properties without memorizing color codes.

myContribution.title: 🚀 My Contribution
myContribution.content: After observing potential pain points in the design-development workflow during collaboration, I proactively proposed implementing Design Tokens to management. Upon approval, I conducted research and collaborated with designers and management to establish a workflow suited to team needs, held sharing sessions to explain implementation from a frontend perspective, successfully piloted the system in projects, and improved design-development collaboration efficiency.
